subject: History
topic: Vedic age — society, polity, religion — mixed tiers
description: Early vs Later Vedic, Sabha Samiti, varna system, four Vedas, deities, Aryan migration

questions.stem: The OLDEST and most sacred among the four Vedas is the:

options.option_text: Atharvaveda, with magical and folk elements
Rigveda, containing 1028 hymns to Indo-Aryan deities
Yajurveda, the manual of sacrificial rituals
Samaveda, the songs to be chanted at rituals

questions.explanation: Four Vedas (in order of antiquity): RIGVEDA (oldest, ~1500-1000 BCE; 1,028 hymns in 10 'mandalas' to deities — Indra, Agni, Varuna, Soma), SAMAVEDA (chants), YAJURVEDA (ritual formulas), ATHARVAVEDA (later, includes folk + magical elements). UNESCO Memory of the World register 2007. Each Veda has 4 parts: Samhitas (hymns), Brahmanas (ritual texts), Aranyakas (forest texts), Upanishads (philosophy). Memory transmitted orally for millennia with extreme accuracy via 'pathas' (recitation methods).

questions.stem: The MAIN occupation in the EARLY VEDIC PERIOD (Rigvedic, ~1500-1000 BCE) was:

options.option_text: Settled agriculture with iron tools used widely
Pastoralism (cattle-rearing) and limited agriculture
Long-distance trade by sea with foreign nations
Iron-smelting industries and complex urban crafts

questions.explanation: Early Vedic — semi-nomadic pastoralists. CATTLE = primary measure of wealth ('gomat' = wealthy = owner of cattle). 'Yuddha' (war) literally meant 'fight for cows'. Rigveda has many hymns about cattle. Late Vedic period (~1000-600 BCE) saw shift to settled AGRICULTURE (iron tools — the 'Iron Age' shift), expansion eastward into Ganga plains, varna stratification, urbanisation. Distractor 1, 3, 4 describe later periods.

questions.stem: Two important POPULAR ASSEMBLIES of the early Vedic age were:

options.option_text: Maha Sabha and Lok Sabha as later constitutional forms
Sabha (council of elders) and Samiti (general assembly)
Mantri Parishad and Council of advisers under the king
Gana and Sangha, the early republican-state forms

questions.explanation: Early Vedic polity: TRIBAL CHIEF (rajan/raja), assisted by: SABHA — council of elders, restricted membership, advisory body. SAMITI — larger general assembly, all adult tribesmen, where the rajan was sometimes elected and approved. VIDATHA — religious + economic council. Both Sabha and Samiti became less important in the Later Vedic period as monarchy strengthened. Distractor 4 (Gana / Sangha) — ancient republican states like Vajji, but these are POST-Vedic (Mahajanapada period).

questions.stem: The most PROMINENT deity in the Rigveda, with the most hymns dedicated to him, is:

options.option_text: Vishnu, the preserver in later mythology
Indra, the god of thunder and warfare
Shiva, the destroyer in later Hinduism
Brahma, the creator in later cosmology

questions.explanation: INDRA — most-praised in Rigveda, ~250 hymns dedicated. King of gods, thunderbolt-wielder, slayer of Vritra (drought-demon), 'Purandara' (fort-breaker). Reflected the warrior-pastoralist values of early Vedic society. AGNI — second most important (~200 hymns), the fire god, intermediary between humans + gods. VARUNA — guardian of cosmic order (rita). Vishnu, Shiva, Brahma — minor in the Rigveda; gained dominance in later Puranic Hinduism (~500 BCE onward).

questions.stem: The four-fold VARNA system (Brahmana, Kshatriya, Vaishya, Shudra) is mentioned for the first time in the:

options.option_text: Atharvaveda, in its folk-magical hymns
Rigveda's Purusha Sukta hymn (10th mandala)
Manusmriti, written around 200 BCE in Sanskrit
Bhagavad Gita, written around 200 BCE

questions.explanation: PURUSHA SUKTA (Rigveda 10.90) — first explicit mention of four varnas. Allegorical: Brahmana from Purusha's mouth (priests), Kshatriya from arms (warriors), Vaishya from thighs (merchants/farmers), Shudra from feet (servants). Considered a LATER addition (10th mandala is the youngest). MANUSMRITI (~200 BCE-200 CE) elaborated the varna system into a rigid law-code. The 'Purusha Sukta' is also notable for envisioning a divine cosmic Person dismembered to create the universe. Distractor 1 — Atharvaveda has caste mentions but not the original. Distractor 3 = Manusmriti (later codification). Distractor 4 = Gita.

questions.stem: The famous 'Battle of Ten Kings' (Dasarajna), described in the Rigveda, was fought on the banks of which river?

options.option_text: Yamuna, near present-day Delhi region
Parushni (modern Ravi) river in the Punjab area
Ganga, near present-day Varanasi area
Saraswati, the lost ancient mythical river

questions.explanation: Dasarajna — described in Rigveda 7.18 — battle between Bharatas (under Sudas, with priest Vasishtha) and a confederation of 10 tribes (under priest Vishvamitra) on the banks of PARUSHNI (modern RAVI) river. Sudas of the Bharata tribe won. The 'Bharata' tribe gave its name to BHARAT — original India. Considered one of the earliest references to the political geography of north-west India in literature.

questions.stem: GAYATRI MANTRA — one of the most sacred Vedic verses — appears in which Veda?

options.option_text: Atharvaveda, in a magical-protection chant
Rigveda (3.62.10), composed by sage Vishvamitra
Yajurveda, in a household ritual section
Samaveda, in a melodic chanting section

questions.explanation: Gayatri Mantra — Rigveda 3.62.10. 'Om bhur bhuvah svah, tat savitur varenyam, bhargo devasya dhimahi, dhiyo yo nah prachodayat.' Composed by sage VISHVAMITRA. Addressed to the solar deity Savitr. 24 syllables in the Gayatri meter (3 lines of 8 syllables). Considered the most sacred Vedic mantra. Recitation is part of daily Brahminical practice + sandhya rituals.
